extracted.intended_audience: authors of general physical histories / popular-science writers and natural philosophers preparing broad expositions of the universe
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for composing a physical history of the universe (or similar popular scientific treatise): how to balance detailed observation and generalization, make science accessible without superficiality, and preserve empirical grounding while achieving elevated, clear exposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish observer's disposition from resulting views
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not confound the disposition of mind in the observer at the time he is pursuing his labors, with the ulterior greatness of the views resulting from investigation and the exercise of thought.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The immediate mental state (e.g., the measured, unromantic labor of precise observation) should not be taken as indicative of the profundity of the conclusions. Laborious, detail-oriented work (meridian altitudes, counting floral parts, angular measurements) can give rise to imposing, elevated general views; precision in observation is the guarantee of sound results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accumulate detailed empirical observations as foundation for generalization
rubrics_metrics.description: The multiplied angular measurements on the one hand, and the detail of organic relations on the other, alike aid in preparing the way for the attainment of higher views of the laws of the universe.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage patient, repeated measurements and the collection of specific facts across disciplines; these isolated facts, when combined by reason, permit the tracing of mutual relations and the discovery of more general laws.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separate the general from the special; suppress unnecessary detail
rubrics_metrics.description: The distinction between dissimilar subjects, and the separation of the general from the special, are not only conducive to the attainment of perspicuity in the composition of a physical history of the universe, but are also the means by which a character of greater elevation may be imparted to the study of nature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid overloading exposition with scaffolding of technical minutiae. Present the 'great masses' clearly by removing unnecessary procedural detail (measurement methods, raw observational scaffolding) so that general results—the 'beacon lights of science'—are seen. Beware the German tendency (as criticized here) to make science inaccessible by excessive accumulation of detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make general results intelligible without demanding full technical prerequisites
rubrics_metrics.description: In the work I am preparing on the physical laws of the universe, the greater part of the facts advanced can be made manifest without the necessity of appealing to fundamental views and principles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim to render conclusions and the structure of scientific knowledge comprehensible to non-specialist readers by explaining general results and relations without presenting every supporting technical proof or demonstration (Laplace's 'reduced to the simple solution' is given as a positive example).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ground exposition in rational empiricism rather than pure abstraction
rubrics_metrics.description: The physical history of the universe... does not pretend to rise to the perilous abstractions of a purely rational science of nature, and is simply a 'physical geography, combined with a description of the regions of space and the bodies occupying them.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid reducing phenomena solely to abstract, a priori principles. Base the narrative on facts registered by science and tested by intellectual reasoning—'rational empiricism'—so the work remains connected to observation and experiment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve appropriate depth: distinguish roles of collectors vs exposers
rubrics_metrics.description: We ought to distinguish between him whose task it is to collect the individual details... and him to whom these relations are to be revealed, under the form of general results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that specialists who gather detailed observations must possess technical mastery, while authors synthesizing general views may legitimately omit fine technicalities. Tailor the level of detail to the role and to the reader: collectors need deep specialty; exposers must render relations and generalizations intelligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrate disciplines: emphasize mutual enrichment of sciences
rubrics_metrics.description: In proportion as laws admit of more general application, and as sciences mutually enrich each other, and by their extension become connected together in more numerous and more intimate relations, the development of general truths may be given with conciseness devoid of superficiality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Draw connections across geology, chemistry, natural history, meteorology, optics, electromagnetism, etc., showing how discoveries in one field illuminate others. Use interdisciplinary examples (e.g., voltaic pile links electric, magnetic, chemical phenomena) to support general claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid promulgating superficial half-knowledge and alarmist dogmatism
rubrics_metrics.description: The superficial half-knowledge... which leads to the introduction of vaguely comprehended scientific views into general conversation, also gives rise... to the expression of alarm at the supposed danger of a collision between the celestial bodies, or of disturbance in the climatic relations of our globe.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not allow incomplete or popularized misunderstanding to generate unfounded fears or dogmatic assertions. Present scientific conclusions with caution, appropriate context, and explanation of limits to prevent misinterpretation by the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use historical and concrete examples to illustrate scientific progress
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples chosen from among the phenomena to which special attention has been directed in recent times, will throw additional light upon the preceding considerations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ instructive historical cases (Galvani/voltaic pile, Huygens' polarization, Arago's chromatic polarization, Laplace) and travel/observational narratives to show how isolated facts led to major generalizations and to demonstrate the practical consequences of 'theoretical' discoveries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize and state the limits of physical explanation
rubrics_metrics.description: All that exceeds this (discovering laws and tracing progressive generalization) goes beyond the province of the physical description of the universe, and appertains to a range of higher speculative views.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be explicit about what physical science can and cannot explain; avoid overstepping into speculative metaphysics. Cite philosophical authorities (e.g., Kant) when delineating the proper bounds of empirical explanation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Present science accessibly yet with dignity and seriousness
rubrics_metrics.description: I take pleasure in persuading myself that scientific subjects may be treated of in language at once dignified, grave, and animated, and that those who are restricted within the circumscribed limits of ordinary life... may thus have opened to them one of the richest sources of enjoyment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write in clear, elevated prose that respects the reader's intellect. Avoid both flippant simplification and impenetrable technicality; aim to awaken interest and understanding across social classes while preserving scientific integrity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value all branches of natural science equally in exposition
rubrics_metrics.description: A more accurate knowledge of the connection of physical phenomena will also tend to remove the prevalent error that all branches of natural science are not equally important in relation to general cultivation and industrial progress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid arbitrarily privileging certain disciplines (mathematics vs natural history vs electro-magnetism). Show how 'theoretical' investigations can yield practical benefits and technological advances, using concrete demonstrations (e.g., voltaic discoveries leading to chemical and analytical tools).

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourage scientifically informed travel and observation
rubrics_metrics.description: It has at length been fully acknowledged... that the narratives of distant travels, too long occupied in the mere recital of hazardous adventures, can only be made a source of instruction where the traveler is acquainted with the condition of the science he would enlarge, and is guided by reason in his researches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When incorporating travelogues and field observations, ensure travelers are versed in the relevant science and guided by reason so that their accounts contribute reliable facts for generalization rather than anecdote.

rubrics_metrics.name: Let the growth of facts suggest new laws and avenues of inquiry
rubrics_metrics.description: The discovery of each separate law of nature leads to the establishment of some other more general law, or at least indicates to the intelligent observer its existence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame exposition to show how each finding points to further generalizations and unresolved problems (e.g., meteorology, radiating heat, parts of optics, electro-magnetism), thereby motivating continued research and honest presentation of scientific limits.
